# Adjudication Task — Chapter 591

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃591화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|뚜. 뚜. 뚜.
  6|
  7|스마트폰 너머로 한참이나 이어지던 연결음이 어느 순간 뚝 끊겼다.
  8|
  9|동시에 기다리던 누군가의 목소리 대신, 익숙하면서도 여전히 낯선 여성의 음성이 귓가를 파고들었다.
 10|
 11|- 연결이 되지 않아, 삐 소리 후 소리샘으로 연결되오며…….
 12|
 13|평소였다면 끊었을 거다. 아니, 전화도 하지 않았을 거다.
 14|
 15|하지만 중년인은 어렴풋이 짐작하고 있었다. 지금 녹음될 자신의 목소리가, 어쩌면 가족에게 남기는 유언이 될지도 모른다는 사실을.
 16|
 17|삐이.
 18|
 19|신호가 시작되었지만, 차마 입술이 떨어지지 않았다.
 20|
 21|무슨 말을 해야 할까. 둘째를 배 속에 품은 아내와 이제 겨우 네 살이 된 자식에게.
 22|
 23|그리고 중년인, 고세원이 고심 끝에 입을 열려던 순간이었다.
 24|
 25|구구구궁.
 26|
 27|건물 전체를 울리는 미세한 진동과 함께, 밖에서 대기하고 있던 경호팀원의 목소리가 문 틈새 사이로 흘러들어왔다.
 28|
 29|“팀장님, 가 보셔야 할 것 같습니다.”
 30|
 31|“…….”
 32|
 33|“팀장님?”
 34|
 35|“기다려, 나간다.”
 36|
 37|짤막한 대답과 함께 고세원은 통화를 종료했다.
 38|
 39|그래, 어쩌면 이건 누군가의 계시인지도 모른다. 죽지 말고 살아남아서 가족들을 만나라는 계시.
 40|
 41|만약 그게 아니라면…….
 42|
 43|‘유언조차 남길 자격이 없다는 거겠지.’
 44|
 45|내심 씁쓸하게 중얼거린 고세원은 문을 열었다. 딱딱하고 무미건조한, 익숙한 얼굴의 경호팀원이 그를 기다리고 있었다.
 46|
 47|“죄송합니다. 다름이 아니라 밖에서…….”
 48|
 49|“알아, 가지.”
 50|
 51|담담하게 말을 끊은 고세원이 발걸음을 옮겼다. 조명이 꺼진 복도를 가로지른 그는 곧 볼 수 있었다.
 52|
 53|최상층에 걸맞은 거대한 원형 홀과 완전 무장을 갖춘 일백여 명의 최정예 길드원들을.
 54|
 55|그리고…… 홀 안을 가득 메우며 뿜어져 나온 홀로그램 영상을.
 56|
 57|- 꽈앙!
 58|
 59|굉음과 함께 섬광이 터져 나오고.
 60|
 61|- 쉬이이잉!
 62|
 63|양 진형에서 솟구친 빛줄기가 서로를 향해 쏘아진다.
 64|
 65|- 크아아악!
 66|
 67|- 탱커어! 대형 정비!
 68|
 69|비명과 고함이 곳곳에서 난무했다. 마치 눈앞에서 벌어지는 것처럼 생생한 그 광경 속에, 서로를 향해 얽혀드는 수백의 헌터가 있었다.
 70|
 71|불과 몇 분 전까지만 하더라도 한 길드에 소속되어 있던 그들은 적이 되어 싸우고 있었다.
 72|
 73|‘저건.’
 74|
 75|고세원은 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 홀로그램 속에서 벌어지는 치열한 전투를 바라보았다.
 76|
 77|가장 선두에서 활약하고 있는 낯익은 얼굴들은 송천우가 이끄는 계파의 길드 내 중역들이다.
 78|
 79|‘반(反) 아레스라……. 결국 이렇게 되는군.’
 80|
 81|머리가 사라진 몸은 곧 쓰러지기 마련이다.
 82|
 83|하지만 이번만큼은 아니었다. 송천우라는 머리는 제거되었지만, 잘려 나간 자리에서는 그보다 더욱 강력한 머리가 자라났다.
 84|
 85|그렇기에 사형 선고를 받은 몸뚱어리가 일어날 수 있었던 것이다.
 86|
 87|홀로그램 영상 속, 인간과 몬스터의 핏물을 뒤집어쓴 채 걸어 나오는 청년이 바로 저들의 새로운 구심점이었다.
 88|
 89|“괴물…….”
 90|
 91|홀로그램을 바라보던 누군가가 신음처럼 중얼거린 그 순간. 청년, 진태경을 중심으로 청백색의 겁화(劫火)가 타올랐다.
 92|
 93|- 화륵. 콰아아아아!
 94|
 95|한 줄기의 불꽃이 사방을 불사르며 공간을 가로질렀다.
 96|
 97|크고 단단한 타워 실드가 산산조각 나며 부서지고, 철벽처럼 버티고 있던 수십여 명의 탱커가 동시에 튕겨져 나가자 팽팽하게 유지되던 균형이 단번에 무너졌다.
 98|
 99|- 크아아악!
100|
101|- 지금이다! 쳐!
102|
103|솟구치는 핏물과 쓰러지는 사람들 사이, 단숨에 한 개의 레이드 팀을 무력화시킨 불꽃은 멈추지 않고 계속해서 쏘아졌다.
104|
105|- 쐐애애애액!
106|
107|그것은 꺼지지 않는 불꽃이었고, 막을 수 없는 유성이었다.
108|
109|폭격도 견딜 수 있다는 천장이 도미노처럼 무너지고 층층이 대기하고 있던 병력들이 짚단처럼 쓰러졌다.
110|
111|불꽃이 움직이는 속도를 따라가지 못한 홀로그램 영상이 잠시 흔들리면, 그는 이미 새로운 층에서 새로운 적들을 쓰러트리고 있었다.
112|
113|- 마, 막……!
114|
115|- 꽈아아앙!
116|
117|그 어떤 것으로도 막을 수 없는 압도적인 무력. 진태경은 한 줄기의 불꽃이 되어 막힘없이 쏘아졌다.
118|
119|층층이 대기하고 있던 병력들이 속절없이 무너져 내리자, 아직까지도 반신반의하며 결정을 내리지 못하던 송천우 계파의 중역들이 마침내 무기를 거꾸로 들었다.
120|
121|- 여, 여기는 85층! 김종필 상무와 13팀이 배반. 컥!
122|
123|- 본부 응답하라! 97층에서 반란이……!
124|
125|- 쉬이이잉, 퍼엉!
126|
127|물살이 강해지면 파도가 되고, 눈덩이는 구를수록 그 크기를 부풀리는 법.
128|
129|현재의 상황이 바로 그랬다. 거세게 타오른 불길이 한 방향을 벗어나 사방으로 번져나가고 있었다.
130|
131|그리고 고세원은 알고 있었다. 분노를 가라앉히기 전까지, 끝끝내 한 사람을 집어삼키기 전까지 진태경이라는 불꽃은 꺼지지 않을 것이라는 사실을.
132|
133|“표, 표적이 100층을 돌파했습니다!”
134|
135|“열두 개 층에서 동시다발적으로 교전이 일어나는 중입니다. 위험 분자들이 표적에게 합류하여 아군과 맞서고 있습니다!”
136|
137|“표적이 홀로 움직입니다! 103층! 아니, 104층으로 진입했습니다!”
138|
139|다급한 외침이 사방에서 빗발친다. 처음 최상층으로 불려 왔을 때만 해도 여유롭던 중역들의 얼굴은 어느덧 초조함으로 물들어 있었다.
140|
141|“이, 이봐. 고 팀장. 하나만 물어봐도 되겠나?”
142|
143|고세원은 홀로그램 영상에서 눈을 떼지 않은 채 대답했다.
144|
145|“말씀하십시오, 최 전무님.”
146|
147|“아까부터 궁금했던 건데 말이야…….”
148|
149|꿀꺽.
150|
151|목울대가 일렁린다. 마른침을 삼킨 반백의 최 전무가 모두의 의문을 대신해 입을 열었다.
152|
153|“도대체. 도대체 부길드장님은 어디 계신 건가?”
154|
155|고세원은 문득 고개를 돌려 주위를 바라보았다. 일백에 달하는 이들 중, 누구보다 앞서 싸워야 할 한 사람의 얼굴은 어디에도 보이지 않았다.
156|
157|그러나 암담한 현실과는 반대로 마음은 오히려 더욱 홀가분해진다.
158|
159|‘그래. 이것으로 된 거겠지.’
160|
161|물라면 물었고, 짖으라면 짖었다.
162|
163|대격변이 낳은 수많은 전쟁 고아 중 하나였던 자신이 지금의 위치에 오를 수 있었던 것은 충실한 사냥개로 살았기 때문이었다.
164|
165|참으로 아이러니하게도, 그 사실이 스스로를 역겹게 만들었다.
166|
167|‘이것을 마지막으로 그간의 빚은 모두 갚았다. 이제 내가 죽건, 살건 더 이상 당신이랑은 아무 상관도 없어.’
168|
169|끝끝내 나타나지 않는 누군가를 향해 마음속으로 뇌까린 고세원은 힘주어 검자루를 뽑았다.
170|
171|스르릉.
172|
173|날선 소음 사이로 담담한 목소리가 섞여들었다.
174|
175|“부길드장님은…… 그는 오지 않을 겁니다.”
176|
177|“뭐, 뭐라고?”
178|
179|“그러니 살고 싶거든 싸우십시오. 여러분이 그 동안 받아 먹은 먹이는 이제 와서 토해 낼 수 없을 만큼 많으니까.”
180|
181|이 자리의 모두가 사냥개다. 주인이 주는 먹이를 받아 먹으며 풍요로운 삶을 영위해 온 그들에게, 더 이상의 선택권은 없었다.
182|
183|‘그래, 나도 마찬가지지.’
184|
185|문득 실소를 흘리는 고세원의 모습에 중역들이 눈을 부릅뜬 그때, 비명 같은 외침이 거대한 홀을 쩌렁쩌렁 울렸다.
186|
187|“119층! 표적이 119층을 돌파했습니다!”
188|
189|“……!”
190|
191|“……!”
192|
193|그 말의 의미를 이해하지 못하는 사람은 없었다.
194|
195|적어도 자신들이 매일같이 출근하는 이 초고층 빌딩이, 120층으로 이루어져 있다는 것 정도는 모두가 알고 있었으니까.
196|
197|‘온다, 그가.’
198|
199|피할 수 없는 싸움.
200|
201|전신 갑주를 착용한 채 한 손에는 검을, 다른 한 손에는 창을 쥔 고세원이 무거운 마음으로 입을 열었다.
202|
203|“포메이션. 전투 준비.”
204|
205|나직한 목소리가 일백명의 귓가를 파고든 그 순간.
206|
207|구구구궁! 콰앙!
208|
209|거대한 진동을 동반한 굉음과 함께, 세계에서 손꼽히는 마천루(摩天樓)가 흔들렸다.
210|
211|지금껏 그 누구도 도전할 수 없었고, 도전하지 않았던 철옹성의 최상층에 초대받지 않은 손님이 발을 디뎠다.
212|
213|저벅.
214|
215|피어오른 먼지 구름 사이로 보이는 한 사람의 인영.
216|
217|고세원은 전신의 털이 곤두서는 듯한 감각과 함께, 온힘을 다해 손에 쥐고 있던 창을 흩뿌렸다.
218|
219|후웅, 쐐애애애액!
220|
221|
222|
223|* * *
224|
225|
226|
227|스걱!
228|
229|나를 향해 쇄도하던 창 한 자루가 먼지구름과 함께 갈라진다.
230|
231|백염이 그린 궤적을 따라 깨끗해진 시야 너머, 왠지 낯익은 중년인의 얼굴이 눈에 들어왔다.
232|
233|‘어디서 봤더라.’
234|
235|의문과 동시에 얼마 되지 않은 기억이 뇌리를 스친다.
236|
237|이정룡의 국가장이 치러지던 그때, 석고준의 곁을 그림자처럼 지키던 새로운 경호팀장. 그것이 바로 중년인의 정체였다.
238|
239|그때 지나가듯 들었던 이름이 아마…….
240|
241|“고세원.”
242|
243|나직한 부름에 중년인. 고세원의 눈동자가 가늘게 떨렸다.
244|
245|그것이 내가 그의 이름을 알고 있기 때문인지, 아니면 앞서의 공격을 너무나도 쉽게 파훼했는지는 모르겠다.
246|
247|다만 확실한 건 드디어 내 질문에 제대로 된 대답을 해 줄 만한 놈을 찾았다는 것이다.
248|
249|나는 로비에서부터 지금까지 수십 번도 넘게 던진 그 질문을 다시 한 번 입에 담았다.
250|
251|“석고준. 어디 있어?”
252|
253|말이 끝나기도 전에 고세원의 손에서 섬광이 뻗어 나왔다.
254|
255|쐐애애액, 쾅!
256|
257|간발의 차로 빗나간 투척용 창이 작은 크레이터를 만들며 틀어박힌다. 그리고 그것이 신호였다.
258|
259|쉬쉬쉬쉭!
260|
261|마지막 최상층에서 나를 기다리고 있던 것은 고세원뿐만이 아니었다.
262|
263|거대한 홀을 메운 백여 명의 아레스 길드원. 한 사람, 한 사람이 상위 헌터라 부르기에 부족함 없는 그들이 일제히 공격을 퍼부었다.
264|
265|화아악!
266|
267|거대한 기가 요동쳤다. 홀 내부가 푸르고, 붉고, 환한 빛으로 가득 찼다.
268|
269|지금까지와는 비교할 수도 없는 위력과 촘촘한 화망(火網)을 갖춘 공격 앞에서, 나는 홀로 걸음을 내디뎠다.
270|
271|저벅. 공력이 실린 발끝이 지면을 밟음과 동시에 피어오른 불꽃이 공기를 뜨겁게 달군다.
272|
273|‘염화일로(炎火一路).’
274|
275|화륵, 쐐애애애액!
276|
277|단 한 걸음이면 족했다. 십 수 미터의 공간을 지워 버린 나는 허공을 향해 일장을 후려쳤다.
278|
279|청백색의 겁화 앞에 화살이 녹아내리고, 허공을 격하고 날아들던 마법이 모조리 해제되었다.
280|
281|퍼엉!
282|
283|물, 땅, 바람, 화염.
284|

*Cough.*

“……”

*What’s this?*

“Now kill—”

Bzzzz.

*Tap. Bzzzz.*

“……”

“……?”

[P273]
“You—”

*KABOOM!*

[P277]
But I was an outlaw. I didn’t need permission.

[P278]
*There.*

[P279]
Everything had a flow.

[P280]
I took a deep breath and closed my eyes. Blue-white Force burst from the spearhead in my hand and tore through the empty air.

[P281]
*Swoooooosh!*

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

A humorless laugh escaped Go Se-won. The executives stared at him.

[P92]
Then a cry rang through the enormous hall.

[P93]
“The 119th floor! The target has broken through the 119th floor!”

[P94]
“……!”

[P95]
“……!”

[P96]
No one had trouble understanding what that meant. They all knew the building they came to work in every day had 120 floors.

[P97]
*He’s coming.*

[P98]
There was no avoiding the fight.

[P99]
Clad in full armor, a sword in one hand and a spear in the other, Go Se-won spoke with a heavy heart.

[P100]
“Formation. Prepare for battle.”

[P101]
His quiet command reached the hundred Hunters around him.

[P102]
Rumble! KABOOM!

[P103]
A tremendous shock shook one of the world’s tallest skyscrapers.

[P104]
An uninvited guest had set foot on the top floor of an impregnable fortress no one had ever been able—or dared—to challenge.

[P105]
*Step.*

[P106]
A lone figure appeared through the rising dust.

[P107]

[P108]
*Whoosh! Screeeeeech!*

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
*Slice!*

[P111]

[P112]
Through the clear path White Flame had cut, I saw a middle-aged man who looked strangely familiar.

*Where have I seen him?*

“Go Se-won.”

“Go Jun. Where is he?”

*Whoosh! KABOOM!*

[P124]

[P126]
*Fwish-fwish-fwish!*

*Fwoosh!*

*Step.*

[P133]
*Flamefire Path.*

[P134]
*Fwoosh! Screeeeeech!*

[P135]

[P136]
Arrows melted before the blue-white hellfire. Every spell flying toward me came apart.

[P137]
*BOOM!*

[P138]
Water, earth, wind, flame.

[P139]

[P140]
*KABOOM!*

[P142]

[P143]
*Pat-pat-pat!*

[P145]
*Killing intent.*

[P146]

[P147]

[P148]
*Screeeeeech!*

[P149]

[P151]
“……!”

[P154]
*Slice!*

[P155]
Blue-white Force extended from White Flame’s spearhead. The incoming weapons lost their strength, and five bodies split in two.

[P157]
*BOOM!*

Compressed air wasn’t the only thing that burst.

[P160]
*Whoosh! Thud!*

Wielded by Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, it buried itself in another man’s neck.

*BOOM!*

[P166]
“Graaaaaah!”

*Crack!*

[P170]
*Fwish! Thud-thud!*

[P172]
“Ghk. Guh…”

[P174]
*You brought this on yourselves.*

[P175]

[P176]

[P177]
*I have to show them here. Make sure this never happens again.*

[P178]

[P179]
That was why I hadn’t been able to eliminate Go Jun in Sichuan. Unlike Lee Jungryong, whom I could have eliminated amid chaos and destruction, Go Jun had stood behind the protection of the rule of law.

[P180]
But now none of that mattered.

[P181]

[P182]
I would never again see the half-gray-haired old butler who had always spoken to me with a polite, gentle smile.

[P183]
That was why I had come here. Why I had torn down the fence called the rule of law and made myself an outlaw.

[P184]
*Splash.*

[P185]
My blood-soaked footsteps sounded unnaturally loud.

[P186]
A suffocating silence had settled over the vast hall. Everyone stood frozen by the slaughter they had witnessed.

[P187]

[P188]
*Go Se-won.*

[P189]
I turned my head to look for Go Jun’s right hand.

[P190]
A faint, stealthy sound cut through the air.

[P191]
*Whoosh!*

[P192]
I spun and clapped my palms together.

[P193]
*KABOOM!*

[P194]
The sharp sword blade caught between them stopped just above my forehead.

[P195]
Its owner, Go Se-won, spoke calmly.

[P196]
“Looking for me?”

[P197]
“Yeah.”

[P198]
I pressed my palms together harder. The Sword Energy—or rather, Aura—formed from powerful mana yielded to my blue-white Force.

[P199]
Unable to withstand my immense internal energy, the sword glowed red and began to melt.

[P200]
*Drip, drip. Hiss!*

[P201]
As the molten steel struck the floor, I thrust out a hand blazing with heat.

[P202]
*BOOM!*

[P203]
One palm strike was enough. Layer upon layer of defensive Magic shattered, and Go Se-won’s armor broke apart.

[P204]
But the blow that shook him to the core didn’t bring him down. He swallowed the blood rising in his throat and reached for my shoulder with his gauntlet.

[P205]
He tried to, anyway.

[P206]
*Tap-tap-tap! BOOM!*

[P207]
I flowed into a grappling technique, and another burst of heat drove him back. He extended his hand.

[P208]
*Fwish!*

[P209]
A blade sprang from between the plates of his gauntlet and grazed my chin. I felt a sting, caught his wrist, and twisted.

[P210]
*Crack! KRAK!*

[P211]
My grip crushed the gauntlet. Flesh tore, exposing white bone.

[P212]
The pain must have been worse than he’d imagined, but Go Se-won didn’t scream. Pale-faced, he asked flatly,

[P213]
“Is that it?”

[P214]
“No. Not yet.”

[P215]
I caught his other arm.

[P216]
*KRAK!*

[P217]
He sucked in a breath.

[P218]
This time the pain broke through his composure. Blood ran between his lips, and his voice shook.

[P219]
“Enough… Finish it.”

[P220]
“I will. After you tell me where that bastard Go Jun is.”

[P221]
“What if the confidentiality clause in my employment contract says I can’t?”

[P222]
I gripped his collarbone.

[P223]
“Then ‘enough’ won’t be where it ends.”

[P224]
Go Se-won gave a weak laugh.

[P225]
“You searched everywhere and still couldn’t find him. Of course you couldn’t.”

[P226]
Unfortunately, he was right. I’d fought my way through an endless pack of hunting dogs and wrecked the inside of the building, but Go Jun had never appeared.

[P227]
The one useful thing I’d learned was that he had a secret place to stay.

[P228]
“Area A. I think you know where it is.”

[P229]
*Cough.*

[P230]
Go Se-won spat blood.

[P231]
“I picked a bad day. I was planning to hand in my resignation soon.”

[P232]
“Enough talking. Tell me.”

[P233]
“That’s easy. But I have a condition.”

[P234]
“T-Team Leader Go. You’re not going to tell that crazy bastard—!”

[P235]
There was always someone who couldn’t read the room. The nameless executive who stepped forward soon went quiet, though. Few people could go on talking after taking Finger Qi to the throat.

[P236]
“A condition?” I asked.

[P237]
“Yes.”

[P238]
What he said next caught even me off guard.

[P239]
“…You want me to kill you?”

[P240]
Go Se-won gave a small nod. Pain made his body tremble, but his eyes remained calm as they met mine.

[P241]
“It’s too late to go back to how things were. Do it cleanly. Right here. That’s all.”

[P242]
“……”

[P243]
“You understand.”

[P244]
Breathing hard, he raised a trembling finger and pointed.

[P245]
When I finally learned where Area A was, I stopped short.

[P246]
*Empty air?*

[P247]
It was hard to make sense of at first, but the world called things like this Magic. Besides, I’d experienced things far stranger and more dangerous than Magic.

[P248]
*Where?*

[P249]
I stared into the empty air. After a moment, an unfamiliar sensation stirred in my exhausted body.

[P250]
*What’s this?*

[P251]
I couldn’t see it. But I could feel another space there, surrounded by an immense, carefully concealed energy.

[P252]
It was hidden so perfectly that I would never have noticed it without knowing it existed.

[P253]
Go Se-won had kept his end of the bargain. His lips, turning blue, began to move.

[P254]
“Now kill—”

[P255]
Bzzzz.

[P256]
A vibration cut him off.

[P257]
A smartphone slipped from the trouser pocket of the suit exposed beneath his broken armor and rolled across the floor.

[P258]
*Tap. Bzzzz.*

[P259]
A family photo lit up its cracked screen beneath the caller’s name: **Wife**.

[P260]
A young child and his wife smiled brightly. Beside them stood Go Se-won, his expression stiff.

[P261]
“……”

[P262]
For a moment, neither of us spoke. I looked from the photo on the cracked screen to the cracks showing in his expression.

[P263]
I remembered his request to be killed. The calm way he’d said it was too late to go back.

[P264]
“Let me ask you something.”

[P265]
“……?”

[P266]
“Why is today your last day at work?”

[P267]
Go Se-won hesitated, then answered with a sigh.

[P268]
“Turns out the job doesn’t suit me. Especially… my boss is a fucking asshole.”

[P269]
“Yeah. I understand.”

[P270]
Did Go Se-won know that answer had decided his fate?

[P271]
I quietly drew up my internal energy.

[P272]
Not into my fist. Into my legs.

[P273]
“You—”

[P274]
*KABOOM!*

[P275]
The rest of his words vanished beneath the roar.

[P276]
I was already soaring into the empty air high above. Fierce wind rushed past me. I felt the strange buoyancy of being seized by invisible hands, and the unknown space that refused entry to anyone without permission.

[P277]
But I was an outlaw. I didn’t need permission.

[P278]
*There.*

[P279]
Everything had a flow.

[P280]
I took a deep breath and closed my eyes. Blue-white Force burst from the spearhead in my hand and tore through the empty air.

[P281]
*Swoooooosh!*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

“Graaaaaah!”

[P50]
“Now! Attack!”

*Screeeeeech!*

[P62]

*Shing.*

“……!”

“……!”

[P184]
*Splash.*

My blood-soaked footsteps sounded unnaturally loud.

*Whoosh!*

[P193]

[P200]
*Drip, drip. Hiss!*

[P202]
*BOOM!*

*Tap-tap-tap! BOOM!*

*Fwish!*

[P216]
*KRAK!*

[P228]
“Area A. I think you know where it is.”

[P229]
*Cough.*

[P230]
Go Se-won spat blood.

[P231]
“I picked a bad day. I was planning to hand in my resignation soon.”

[P232]
“Enough talking. Tell me.”

[P233]
“That’s easy. But I have a condition.”

[P234]
“T-Team Leader Go. You’re not going to tell that crazy bastard—!”

[P235]

[P236]
“A condition?” I asked.

[P237]
“Yes.”

[P238]

[P239]
“…You want me to kill you?”

[P240]
Go Se-won gave a small nod. Pain made his body tremble, but his eyes remained calm as they met mine.

[P241]
“It’s too late to go back to how things were. Do it cleanly. Right here. That’s all.”

[P242]
“……”

[P243]
“You understand.”

[P244]
Breathing hard, he raised a trembling finger and pointed.

[P245]
When I finally learned where Area A was, I stopped short.

[P246]
*Empty air?*

[P247]
It was hard to make sense of at first, but the world called things like this Magic. Besides, I’d experienced things far stranger and more dangerous than Magic.

[P248]
*Where?*

[P249]
I stared into the empty air. After a moment, an unfamiliar sensation stirred in my exhausted body.

[P250]
*What’s this?*

[P251]
I couldn’t see it. But I could feel another space there, surrounded by an immense, carefully concealed energy.

[P252]
It was hidden so perfectly that I would never have noticed it without knowing it existed.

[P253]
Go Se-won had kept his end of the bargain. His lips, turning blue, began to move.

[P254]
“Now kill—”

[P255]
Bzzzz.

[P256]

[P257]
A smartphone slipped from the trouser pocket of the suit exposed beneath his broken armor and rolled across the floor.

[P258]
*Tap. Bzzzz.*

[P259]
A family photo lit up its cracked screen beneath the caller’s name: **Wife**.

[P260]
A young child and his wife smiled brightly. Beside them stood Go Se-won, his expression stiff.

[P261]
“……”

For a moment, neither of us spoke. I looked from the photo on the cracked screen to the cracks showing in his expression.

[P263]
I remembered his request to be killed. The calm way he’d said it was too late to go back.

[P264]
“Let me ask you something.”

[P265]
“……?”

[P266]
“Why is today your last day at work?”

“Turns out the job doesn’t suit me. Especially… my boss is a fucking asshole.”

[P269]
“Yeah. I understand.”

I quietly drew up my internal energy.

[P272]
Not into my fist. Into my legs.

[P273]
“You—”

[P274]
*KABOOM!*

[P275]
The rest of his words vanished beneath the roar.

[P276]

[P277]
But I was an outlaw. I didn’t need permission.

[P278]
*There.*

[P279]
Everything had a flow.

[P280]
I took a deep breath and closed my eyes. Blue-white Force burst from the spearhead in my hand and tore through the empty air.

[P281]
*Swoooooosh!*

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
